name: beat-triton-fusion
title: Beat Triton on the elementwise front via automatic pointwise fusion
description: Demonstrate IntentIR's performance advantage: recover the algebra of a pointwise chain from lifted intent and emit it as ONE fused, tiled GPU kernel that beats the unfused Triton/library composition. DoD: a memory-bound chain (e.g. silu(a)*b+c, the SwiGLU FFN) compiles to exactly one kernel, certifies vs torch (rel<1e-3), and beats the unfused Triton baseline at HBM-bound sizes; honest GB/s + a hand-fused-Triton tie column; corpus/PERF_FUSION.md.
creator: kingdom
notes: DONE. The 983x flash gap was one-thread-per-query; the fix for the elementwise front is automatic fusion, not just tiling. Gating fact: -convert-intent-to-linalg emits one linalg.generic per op (N launches, no advantage); adding -linalg-fuse-elementwise-ops collapses a pointwise chain to ONE linalg.generic -> ONE gpu kernel (verified by launch count). The default scf.parallel->gpu maps each element to its own BLOCK (threads (1,1,1)); -scf-parallel-loop-tiling=parallel-loop-tile-sizes=1,256 makes the inner contiguous dim a 256-thread coalesced block. compile_all_kernels_fused(tile) + run_program(compile_all=...) hook. Result (RTX 5090 D, f32, HBM-bound, median-of-5, no per-iter sync): IntentIR auto-fused kernel beats unfused Triton 1.41-1.53x (at the 6:4 traffic ceiling) and TIES a hand-written fused Triton kernel (~1.00x), proving the win is the fusion the library skipped, not a codegen trick. Baselines are clean inline Triton (flag_gems pointwise_dynamic hits the Triton-3.6 launcher arg-count bug at scale). Scope: elementwise front only; the flash latency gap is untouched. Borrowed bench/flash_emit.py's hand-emit + generic-launch pattern.
